text:
maya (AE): Hey all — kickoff for Northbridge POC. They're using CompetitorX and want a drop-in migration. Main unknowns: session stickiness (they rely on server-side session profile + per-session system prompt), prompt parity (we see small response deltas), and enterprise security answers. Timeline: demo next Thu, POC by EOW. Any blockers?
liam - solutions: Quick Q — does CompetitorX keep session state server-side or do clients send full session payload each request? I remember two different flows.
natalie (SE): They use a session_id cookie + session create endpoint where you attach the system prompt. Subsequent generate calls only send session_id and user turns. Example:
```
# CompetitorX session create
POST /v1/sessions
{ "session_id": "sb-123", "system_prompt": "You are a helpful assistant", "ttl": 86400 }
# generate
POST /v1/generate
{ "session_id": "sb-123", "input": "Summarize X" }
```
liam - solutions: Thanks. Redwood's hosted API is stateless per-request but we have conversation support via `conversation_id` and optional `initial_prompt` on the first call and we also support prefix caching + KV cache on runtime side. For the POC we can emulate CompetitorX behavior by creating a short-lived mapping shim that issues a `conversation_id` and stores the system prompt server-side.
alex (sales-eng): Customer cares about "session stickiness" because they do reranking + tool-calling inside the session and expect deterministic continuation. Can we guarantee the same KV cache keys across model variants?
natalie (SE): We can. Implementation notes: map CompetitorX `session_id` -> Redwood `conversation_id`. Attach original system_prompt into the first call metadata. We recommend pinning model_revision for the POC to reduce variability (e.g., `redwood/gemini-v2:2026-03-01`). Also enable prefix-cache for the first 2 turns.
security-eng: For ent security: we support VPC Private deployment (control plane optional), KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2/ISO reports under NDA. We'll need the customer's security questionnaire filled; send them this link: https://redwood.internal/sec-qa (placeholder). Also note: we can't extract their on-prem session store without a Private deployment.
maya (AE): Northbridge asked also about billing differences — they currently pay per-conversation-turn at CompetitorX. They want to know per-token vs per-turn impact and Dedicated reserved capacity options.
liam - solutions: Rough guidance: per-turn billing usually maps to more predictable monthly spend if turns and tokens are stable. With Redwood hosted API we bill per-token for generation + per-embedding for embeddings. For Dedicated we can offer committed monthly throughput (GPU pool) + predictable per-token tiers and flat overage. I'll prepare a quick cost model for their typical workload (30M input tokens/month, avg 120 tokens/turn, ~250k turns).
alex (sales-eng): Also they have a security blocker: legal needs evidence of private key handling for customer-managed KMS, and a signed data processing addendum plus flow for MSA countersign. Any checklist items?
security-eng: Checklist for Private/Dedicated: 1) KMS integration doc (HSM/Cloud KMS). 2) Network diagram + required IP allowlist. 3) Audit log retention options. 4) SOC2 reports + DPA. We can turn around docs in 48-72h after NDA.
maya (AE): POC acceptance criteria from customer: parity on 5 canonical prompts, <=5% semantic divergence on rerank outputs, no auth flow changes for client apps. Can we run automated evals?
natalie (SE): Yes — suggest we create an eval set of their 5 prompts + 20 variants, run both CompetitorX and Redwood pinned model, compute embedding cosine similarity + BLEU-like fuzz. I can script this. Example eval command:
```
# pseudo-eval
python eval_parity.py --src competitorx_results.json --target redwood_results.json --metrics cosine,bleu,f1
```
devex-bot: Reminder: create a short-lived staging workspace for Northbridge: workspace-id `nb-poc-2026` and grant `natalie (SE)` + `liam - solutions` access.
ops-oncall: If we need to emulate CompetitorX rate headers, they use `X-Rate-Remaining` + `X-Rate-Reset`. Redwood returns standard `X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining`. We can add compatibility headers in the shim for POC. Note: do not expose internal token TTL values.
maya (AE): Action items: @natalie create eval harness and run parity by Wed; @liam prepare cost model and Dedicated pricing by Wed; @security-eng send sec-qa link + list of required docs; @alex prep SOW talking points and DPA status. Demo scheduled Thu 10am PT.
liam - solutions: I'll also add a small compatibility layer example repo (proxy) that shows mapping `session_id` -> `conversation_id` and header translations. Will post link when ready.
maya (AE): Great — if we hit the parity targets we propose a 2-week alpha on Dedicated. Keeping notes here for legal and PS. :thumbsup:
alex (sales-eng): Noted. I'll call Northbridge legal to align timelines.
security-eng: FYI — if Northbridge insists on on-prem session store access, we must do Private deployment.
maya (AE): Thanks everyone — will update thread with links.
